page: Microsoft Azure L64s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for I/O-intensive workloads. It is built on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provisions 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. A massive 15,360 GB of local NVMe SSD storage is directly bundled with the instance, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present.

Hardware capabilities include advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography extensions (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), supplemented by 260 MB of L3 cache. In benchmark evaluations, multi-core CPU performance ranks in the top tiers, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,563.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 73,408.39. Memory bandwidth reaches 225.0 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 96.91 GB/sec for uncached writes. Database and web throughput tests also reflect superior capacity, with static web serving hitting 93.83 GB/sec and Redis SET operations achieving 78.56 million ops/sec.

The dense pairing of 64 dedicated compute threads with 15.36 TB of fast NVMe storage provides high hardware resource density without requiring external block storage overhead. CPU-based inference remains capable due to AMX extensions, processing up to 3,096.71 tokens per second on small language models, though large model inference drops to average rates due to the lack of dedicated GPUs. The instance is suited for large relational and NoSQL databases, transactional processing, data warehousing, high-throughput caching, and log analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure L64s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) and 512.0 GB of memory. Bundled with 15,360 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and lacking discrete GPUs, the configuration is tailored for data-heavy operations. Benchmark evaluations place the server in top percentiles for multi-core compute and throughput, achieving 21,563.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 78.56 million ops/sec in Redis SET operations, and 93.83 GB/sec in static web serving. Hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX extensions aids vector and matrix processing. The substantial local disk density and high memory bandwidth provide efficient execution for high-throughput transactional databases, large NoSQL clusters, search indices, and heavy data transformation pipelines.
